podcast.body: The Weavers recorded a hit version of his song, "Good Night Irene." "their version of Lead Belly's Good Night Irene, with orchestration by Gordon Jenkins."

podcast.title: Central Figure in New York Folk Scene
podcast.body: Lead Belly was part of a group of left-wing intellectuals and folk singers in New York, centered around Alan Lomax and Pete Seeger, which was pivotal to the Greenwich Village folk scene and the formation of The Armanac Singers and The Weavers. "he hooked up with a group of left-wing intellectuals and folk singers, centering on Alan Lomax, Pete Seeger, and Leab Belly."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Friend of Pete Seeger
podcast.body: Lead Belly was friends with Pete Seeger in the 1940s. "He had been friends with both Woody Guthrie and Lead Belly in the 40s."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 92: "The Lion Sleeps Tonight" by the Tokens

podcast.title: Influence on Dave Van Ronk
podcast.body: Dave Van Ronk's love for folk blues artists like Lead Belly helped transition him from traditional jazz into the folk scene. "he'd started out as a traditional jazz guitarist and banjo player, but had slowly moved on into the folk side of things, through his love of blues singers like Bessie Smith and folk blues artists like Lead Belly."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 97: "Song to Woody" by Bob Dylan

podcast.title: Repertoire for Dylan
podcast.body: Lead Belly's songs were part of Odetta's repertoire, which Bob Dylan learned after his epiphany, performing them with Spider-John Körner. "Dylan had soon sold his electric guitar and bought an acoustic, and he immediately learned all of Odetta's repertoire and started performing her songs and lead bellies with a friend Spider-John Körner"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 97: "Song to Woody" by Bob Dylan

podcast.title: Skiffle Repertoire
podcast.body: His songs were a primary component of the repertoire for skiffle groups, alongside those of Woody Guthrie and Big Bill Broonzy. "a repertoire that was made up primarily of songs by Lead Belly, Woody Guthrie and Big Bill Brunze."
